title: Autotuning CuTe DSL Kernels
critical_patterns: Use grid search for exhaustive exploration of parameter combinations
Random search is faster and often as effective for large parameter spaces
Bayesian optimization uses machine learning to guide the search efficiently
Genetic algorithms evolve configurations over generations
Cache results to avoid redundant tuning
Tune parameters specific to problem sizes for optimal performance
constraints: Ensure configurations respect hardware limits like thread count
Tune on the target hardware to ensure results are applicable
Avoid overtuning by stopping when improvements are marginal
Validate configurations to avoid invalid parameter combinations
compressed_summary: Autotuning in CuTe DSL involves automatically finding optimal kernel parameters by exploring different configurations and measuring performance. Key concepts include defining parameter spaces, employing search strategies like grid, random, Bayesian, and genetic algorithms, and measuring performance to identify the best configurations. Autotuning is critical for adapting to specific hardware and problem sizes, and caching results prevents redundant tuning. Practical patterns include starting with a coarse grid search, refining with more targeted searches, and using problem-size-specific tuning. Constraints include respecting hardware limits, tuning on the target hardware, and avoiding overtuning. Autotuning can significantly improve kernel performance, often finding configurations that are 2-5× better than manual tuning. Best practices involve caching tuned parameters, validating correctness, and using the appropriate strategy for the problem size and hardware. Tools like Bayesian optimization libraries and frameworks like OpenTuner can aid in this process. Overall, autotuning is a powerful method to optimize GPU kernels efficiently, adapting to different hardware and problem sizes automatically.
